modelResponse.episodeSummary: 79F with urosepsis and sepsis-induced tachycardia, presenting with new-onset Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response (RVR).
modelResponse.rhythm: Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response (RVR)
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Narrow QRS, absent P waves, fibrillatory baseline
preEventNote: 'Sinus tachycardia earlier in shift; converted to AFib RVR as fever spiked'
modelResponse.mechanism: Systemic inflammatory response to infection (Urosepsis) causing increased sympathetic tone and metabolic demand, leading to conversion from sinus tachycardia to atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.

rejectedAlternatives.why: Troponin T 0.03 ng/mL is only mildly elevated and does not correlate with acute ischemic changes; primary driver is clearly infectious/septic.
Potassium 3.6 mmol/L is within normal range.
While tachycardia is present, the clinical context strongly favors sepsis/urosepsis as the primary driver.

recommendedActions: Increase norepinephrine dose to maintain MAP > 65 mmHg
Assess for fluid responsiveness and adjust crystalloid infusion
Continue monitoring of heart rate and rhythm
Monitor for further hemodynamic deterioration or worsening of sepsis
uncertainty: Current MAP 67 is borderline; requires close monitoring of trend.
Rhythm conversion is not currently indicated as the patient is hemodynamically unstable (sepsis) and requires stabilization of underlying cause.
